assignments.node_id: מחלקת הן בגשמיות הן ברוחניות שאינו יכול להתפלל או לעשות מה שצריך בעבודת השם. כי הכל בכלל מחלקת, שעומדים וחולקים עליו ורוצים לבטל דעתו ורצונו מה שרוצה לעשות, וכדי לבטל המחלקת מאיזה בחינה שתהיה ולעשות שלום
assignments.reason: This is the elaborated form of מַחֲלֹקֶת (strife), describing all forms of opposition — physical and spiritual — that stand against a person's will and prevent him from serving God. Its essential nature IS strife/alien wills, the same domain as the short-form מַחֲלֹקֶת already in Package 1. It describes the phenomenon of opposing wills in its fullest expression. Neutral polarity because strife itself is the structural reality of clashing wills, not inherently good or evil — it is the problem-state within the will-domain.

assignments.node_id: נכנע ונחלש הלב ונתבטל כל הרצונות האחרים שלו מפני רצון הקדוש־ברוך־הוא, לאדבקא רעותא דלבא וכו
assignments.reason: This describes the inner state where the heart is subdued and all alien desires are nullified before God's will, enabling the heart's desire to cling to the Holy One. Its essential nature is the transformation of רָצוֹן (will) — the positive pole of the will-domain. It is not fasting itself (Package 2) but rather what happens within the will when fasting operates: the will is redirected from self to God. It belongs to Package 1 because it IS a state of ratzon — holy, God-directed will — the positive resolution within the will-domain. Good polarity because this is the will oriented toward God.

assignments.node_id: נתבטל המחלקת שהוא בחינת רצונות אחרים שלא כרצונו
assignments.reason: This is the nullification of strife, explicitly identified as 'בְּחִינַת רְצוֹנוֹת אֲחֵרִים' — the aspect of alien wills. Its essential nature is the dissolution of the machloket/alien-will phenomenon. The node itself names machloket and ratzon as its defining concepts, placing it squarely in the will-domain of Package 1. Good polarity because nullification of strife is the positive outcome — alien wills dissolve before one's own God-aligned will.

assignments.node_id: נתבטל רצונו מפני רצון השם יתברך
assignments.reason: Self-nullification of one's own will before the will of God. This IS ratzon in its purest form — the pivotal act of the teaching where personal will is surrendered to divine will. The Mishnah 'בַּטֵּל רְצוֹנְךָ מִפְּנֵי רְצוֹנוֹ' is the conceptual heart of this node. Its essential nature is entirely within the will-domain (Package 1), not the fasting-domain (Package 2) — fasting is the mechanism, but this concept IS about the will itself being redirected. Good polarity because surrendering to God's will is the supreme positive act in this teaching.

Peace (shalom) in this Torah is defined as the state where all wills are aligned — alien wills have been nullified, and there is no longer machloket. The teaching's logic is: 'מַרְבֶּה צְדָקָה מַרְבֶּה שָׁלוֹם' — peace is the resolution of strife. Its essential nature in THIS Torah is the harmony of wills, the positive end-state of the ratzon-domain. Shalom is not a practice (Package 2) but the state when the will-conflict described in Package 1 reaches resolution. It is the good pole of the will-domain: where machloket is the state of fragmented/opposing wills, shalom is the state of unified/harmonized wills. Good polarity.

assignments.node_id: שמעורר ומחיה מתים, הינו הימים שעברו בחשך, ואין להם שום חיות
assignments.reason: Revival of dead days — days that passed in darkness and lost their vitality. This concept's essential nature is spiritual vivification/restoration of life-force. It is not fasting itself (Package 2 is the practice), nor is it about will/strife (Package 1). It belongs to the domain of vitality and joy — the teaching's second major theme: fasting revives dead days, and from those revived days joy is built. It is the mechanism within the joy/vitality domain. Good polarity because reviving days is a restorative, holy act.

new_packages.label: שִׂמְחָה וְחִיּוּת
new_packages.reason: Torah 179 has two major thematic outcomes: (1) peace through nullification of alien wills (which belongs to the will-domain, Package 1), and (2) joy through revival of dead days (a distinct thematic domain). The teaching devotes lines 6-14 to explaining how fasting revives past days that were spiritually dead, building the 'stature of joy' (קוֹמַת הַשִּׂמְחָה). These three nodes — שִׂמְחָה (joy as the vitality built from revived days), שָׂשׂוֹן וְשִׂמְחָה (the Talmudic pair denoting festive celebration when peace exists), and the revival of dead days (the vivification mechanism) — all share the essential nature of spiritual vitality/life-force restored. They do not belong to Package 1 (will/strife) or Package 2 (fasting/charity as practices). They are the fruit, not the practice or the problem. The verse 'שַׂמְּחֵנוּ כִּימוֹת עִנִּיתָנוּ' (make us rejoice according to the days of our affliction) positions this as a proportional, measurable spiritual reality — a domain in its own right.
